title: Describing People and Reacting to Statements
summary: Talking about people’s appearance and character and reacting in conversation.
whyItMatters: Descriptions help identify someone and exchange impressions, but wording matters. A useful description combines observable details, relevant character information, and reactions that show agreement, uncertainty, or a different perspective.

mentalModel.title: Identify before evaluating
mentalModel.content: Begin with neutral appearance or clothing details that help the listener know who you mean.

mentalModel.title: Support character words with context
mentalModel.content: Instead of only saying 'nett', add a behavior or situation that explains the impression.

mentalModel.title: React without ending the conversation
mentalModel.content: Agree, qualify, or disagree politely and add one reason or question.

ruleBlocks.title: Identify with relevant visible details
ruleBlocks.content: Use clothing, hair, location, or an accessory: 'Die Frau mit der grünen Jacke'.

ruleBlocks.title: Describe character carefully
ruleBlocks.content: Use phrases such as 'Ich finde ihn freundlich' and add evidence or a situation.

ruleBlocks.title: Choose an active reaction
ruleBlocks.content: Use 'Das finde ich auch', 'Wirklich?', 'Vielleicht', or 'Ich sehe das etwas anders'.

ruleBlocks.title: Use comparisons for clarification
ruleBlocks.content: Say 'Er ist größer als Ben' when a comparison helps identify or distinguish someone.

tables.title: Conversation Toolkit
rows: Meinst du die Frau mit der roten Jacke?
Vielleicht, aber heute ist er sehr ruhig.

tables.title: Building a Description
rows: Er ist groß und hat kurze Haare.
Er ist etwas älter als Tom.
Er hilft den neuen Kollegen oft.

sentenceStructure: Use accusative pronouns after the person is established.
Add a reason or example to subjective character descriptions.
Use softening words such as 'vielleicht', 'etwas', and 'eher'.

comparisons.summary: The theme lesson supplies neutral appearance and clothing language.
Comparative forms help distinguish people and qualify observations.

examples.de: A: Wer ist Nora? B: Die Frau mit der grünen Jacke und der Brille.
examples.en: A: Who is Nora? B: The woman with the green jacket and glasses.

examples.de: A: Wie findest du sie? B: Sie wirkt freundlich und sehr ruhig.
examples.en: A: What do you think of her? B: She seems friendly and very calm.

examples.de: A: Paul ist sehr hilfsbereit. B: Ja, das finde ich auch.
examples.en: A: Paul is very helpful. B: Yes, I think so too.

examples.de: A: Er ist immer ernst. B: Ich sehe das etwas anders; er lacht oft.
examples.en: A: He is always serious. B: I see that somewhat differently; he often laughs.

examples.de: Mina ist kleiner als Lea, aber sie trägt den längeren Mantel.
examples.en: Mina is shorter than Lea, but she is wearing the longer coat.

commonMistakes.wrong: Use a harsh label without context.
commonMistakes.correct: Use a neutral observation or soften a personal impression.
commonMistakes.reason: Descriptions should remain relevant and respectful.

commonMistakes.correct: Add agreement, qualification, or a reason.
commonMistakes.reason: An active reaction keeps the exchange meaningful.

specialCases: 'Wirken' expresses an impression rather than a confirmed fact.
'Aussehen' often uses 'wie' or an adjective: 'Sie sieht müde aus'.
Avoid unnecessary comments about sensitive personal characteristics.
tips: Describe fictional or pictured people before real acquaintances.
Practice three reactions to the same statement.
Support one character adjective with a concrete behavior.

sourceStyle.origin: LangCompass editorial lesson aligned to the Momente A1.2 M4 catalog topic
sourceStyle.notes: The lesson combines identification, evidence-based impressions, and socially appropriate reactions.
